axis_coverage.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competing and analogous approaches, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.assessment: This is substantive discovery. It offers a published optional comparison-star binning method with a test-star/cadence/noise discriminator; an analogous large-instrument rotating-illumination study with explicit transfer limits; an integrated AIJ workflow versus transparent ccdproc reduction and separate photometry; standards-based flat validation; and TESS pixel/product scrutiny as an independent instrument route. Local rotation, calibration, revision, timing and environmental histories cannot be recovered without logs, so their retrieval is specifically designed rather than fabricated. The final selects an evidence-gathering order provisionally and keeps astronomical and environmental branches open. It does not substitute a warning list for discovery.

axis_coverage.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: Performed work is identified as document/source research and proposal/critique/revision. No photometry, arithmetic, toy series, archive search, code deployment, telescope action or empirical validation is claimed. Proposed checks discriminate rather than simply rerun: historical and one-factor reductions test implementation sensitivity; standards/check stars assess performance; detector/background/airmass variables test nuisance linkage; leave-one-out ensembles expose reference dependence; observed cadence/window and covariance-aware full-selection simulations address aliases and selection; a controlled angle pilot and suitable external instrument provide stronger discrimination. No one of these is an oracle for intrinsic variability. The final reserves classification until source-centered independent evidence and valid performance/timing controls; inadequate coverage or a mismatched passband makes non-detection inconclusive. Thresholds and observing authorization remain justified external choices because no frames or endpoint are supplied.
limits: No empirical validation occurred; this is appropriate for the synthetic planning assignment, not an invented missing deployment.
A future pilot must choose a design and performance thresholds from the actual camera, archive and endpoint.

urls_versions_and_independent_checks.version: arXiv:1701.04817 expanded 2017 paper; retrieved PDF header inspected
urls_versions_and_independent_checks.semantic_check: AIJ differential flux and its error model need the actual detector gain, dark current and read noise. Ensemble manipulation without repeating aperture extraction is an implementation capability, not independent observations. Circular-aperture support in this old paper does not describe every later release.

urls_versions_and_independent_checks.version: Official legacy guide; self-identifies as very out of date; variable-aperture note names AIJ 2.1.4
urls_versions_and_independent_checks.semantic_check: The FWHM estimate uses pixels inside the initial fixed aperture; that aperture must exceed the largest sequence FWHM. Historical multipliers and the guide itself are not current universal defaults. The final preserves this limitation and recommends recovering the installed version.

The BJD correction is specifically for TESS TICA full-frame images. Generalizing it to ground FITS or all TESS products would be wrong; the candidate does not do so. Other entries document freeform apertures and FITS product handling.

Observatory latitude/longitude header options require the selected keywords and correct values. The release also revises external BJD conversion and carries a specific Prism WCS caveat. Final uses this as dated history, not a claim about the teaching system.

Optional flip detection uses a changing measurement-table value such as PIERSIDE. FITS opening, comparison-column display and plotting changes are explicitly release-specific. The final does not claim these caused the reported pattern.

subtract_dark defaults to no scaling; explicit scale=True and exposure metadata/units are needed for exposure scaling. The worked route assumes a bias-subtracted master dark. flat_correct uses mean normalization by default; its floor is optional. Calibration units must match the post-gain image; uncertainty propagates. The final does not choose scaling for an unidentified CMOS/CCD camera.

The study supports static/rotating illumination tests and star-based flux-scale checks, not transfer of coefficients or a promised improvement. Its full fit needs suitable spatial offsets; rotation alone can leave radial terms degenerate. Coefficients vary with filter and era, and wrong-era application can worsen results. Candidate proposes diagnostic residual comparisons, not this coefficient-fitting algorithm.

Agreement between two flats can coexist with erroneous calibration. Known stars across positions supply an external performance check. The result for the particular dome-screen instrument does not select a universal flat technology here.

Publisher search payload sections 2.5, 3.2, 4.2, 6 and 7 independently inspected after direct open failed. Binning applies to comparison measurements, optimized using a non-varying test star; good conditions, rapid cadence relative to systematics, and unblended sources matter. Rapid-trend intervals can remain unbinned while suitable intervals are binned. The amended final is supported; the original draft blanket-sounding caveat was minor.

urls_versions_and_independent_checks.semantic_check: The documented quality_bitmask accepts strings or integer masks; default ignores severe flags, hard can discard good cadences, hardest is discouraged. flux_column defaults to pdcsap_flux for light-curve products only. The candidate restricts these statements to product reading and distinguishes them from v2.5.0 release history.

urls_versions_and_independent_checks.version: v2.5.0, commit f6c5f1e; changelog heading dated 2024-08-19; GitHub release API publication 2024-08-29T17:15:29Z
urls_versions_and_independent_checks.semantic_check: Tagged release supports named QLP sector-56-and-later reader, short-cadence search and KEPSEISMIC time-format changes. The time-format fix is not a general fix for all TESS clocks. Final makes the historical claim without claiming a local defect, and retains the old releases-list URL explicitly. The 2024-08-19 date is the changelog heading; GitHub publication metadata is 2024-08-29T17:15:29Z. Candidate source maps call the heading a release date, a minor chronology-label imprecision without effect on the selected fixes or proposal.

JD/HJD/BJD location labels do not establish time scale. Preserve site-arrival timing and conversion inputs; exposure midpoint is not always flux-weighted mean under changing flux/transparency. The final requires native shutter convention, clock/site/source coordinates before conversions and claims no achieved timing precision.

urls_versions_and_independent_checks.version: Official Astropy v8.0.1 stable API at independent retrieval
urls_versions_and_independent_checks.semantic_check: Largest-peak FAP estimates depend on a non-varying Gaussian-noise null and search frequency range; methods are approximations (baluev is default), not posterior probability of a true period. PSD normalization also needs supplied errors. Candidate invokes these limits without running a search or treating FAP as a variability classifier.

Structured/nightly windowing causes aliases and harmonics; the largest peak can be wrong. Inspect cadence/window and independent evidence. Candidate does not import the paper simulation percentages into the synthetic case.

Off-diagonal covariance invalidates iid scaling; adjacent-point means can improve less than n^(-1/2). OGLE transit thresholds and millimagnitude noise are study-specific. Candidate transfers residual dependence/RMS diagnostics rather than its thresholds.

The formulation assumes independent Gaussian errors and tests a searched-frequency maximum. Its bound is not automatic correction for stars, aperture/ensemble variants or post-selected candidate rules. Candidate distinguishes full selection/search modeling from per-periodogram FAP.

Calibration removes unwanted signal levels, not their shot noise; calibration-frame noise adds. Matching temperature and applicable CMOS gain/offset/binning/readout is prescribed. Scaled darks isolate bias and assume a scalable response; unscaled raw darks include bias and match exposure. Check stars, standards, color/position trends and independent software support controls. Candidate transfers these checks, not universal camera settings.

The actual Rev F independently exists at a different official MAST URL. Its SPOC scope and distinction between filename UTC conventions and data timing support the proposal generic product/time audit. No Rev-F-only operation is selected in the final. This independent check does not repair the candidate locator.
